ambiguities.text: The spec states 'mid-creation contracts' return the account address itself, but doesn't define precisely when an account is considered 'mid-creation'.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume mid-creation refers to the execution context during a CREATE/CREATE2 operation before the deployment is finalized, where the account has initcode running but no finalized code.

ambiguities.text: The spec does not specify behavior if the delegation target address itself has a delegation.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume EXTCODEADDRESS only resolves one level of delegation. Chained delegations would require multiple calls to fully resolve.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'Only target_address is warmed. If a delegation is found the address that it is delegated to is not added to the accessed_addresses' has implications for gas estimation.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume subsequent operations accessing the delegation target will incur cold access costs unless they warm it themselves.

implicit_assumptions.description: The EIP-7702 delegation mechanism is secure and delegation designations cannot be forged.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attackers could forge delegation designations to bypass security checks in sponsorship or proxy contracts.

implicit_assumptions.description: EOF contracts using EXTCODEADDRESS are deployed in contexts where EIP-7702 delegations exist.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: The opcode would return the original address in most cases, providing limited utility until delegation adoption increases.

implicit_assumptions.description: Contracts relying on EXTCODEADDRESS for security checks will properly handle the case where delegation changes between transactions.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Race conditions where delegation changes during multi-step operations could lead to security vulnerabilities.
